items.note: Association named, organized 1889, Gideon Vose first president, creamery at Larrow Green 1891 - all present.

Article VII given only as 'the test of the station where a man delivered govern his pay'. The bolded payment rule - by the pound of butterfat, ascertained by test, not by the weight of the milk - appears nowhere in Section A (no occurrence of 'butterfat' or 'weight of the milk' in the reconstructions).

Does not state that the pay-by-test rule is what made a wrong test cost money; the consequence it draws is Frick's 'no remedy except to quarrel with a figure', i.e. absence of appeal, not the economic transfer, and never the payment-by-weight counterfactual.

Loomis (secretary 1901, minute book), Wilbur Teague (his ledger/book) and Hobart Sill (Larrow Green, lender of the 1896 glass) all named inside Section A. List item with no REQUIRED line; core fact - the officer roster - is present.

Selby Vose is identified as Gideon's son in Section A, but 'manager from 1913' is absent - the string 1913 does not occur anywhere in the reconstructions. Manager role stated only at B3, which cannot travel into Section A.

The 'station gain' line named and its shape given (fat credited vs fat received at Larrow Green, difference entered as station gain, five and a quarter per cent carried to the general account), with the 1898 ledger origin.
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, first season on glassware borrowed from Larrow Green.

The working of the test system is not described in Section A: no weighing at intake, no composite sample per patron, no percent read on the graduated neck, no cream shipped / skim returned. Only the '8 per cent neck ruled for that one charge' fragment appears.
Ammon & Sons of Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, glass in use from 1 May 1897, with the 1898/1899 rivals rejected on the dated diary entry.
Six dozen milk-test pipettes blown to deliver 17.6 c.c., $77.93, with $77.39 and 'five dozen' identified as misprints.
States the 0.19 shortfall was flat and seasonless - the same nineteen hundredths in the June flush and in February - and draws the instrument-not-feed inference.
Never says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, or that the one unverified object defined the answer. 'Burette' does not occur anywhere in Section A; it appears only at C1(a).

Keddie born 1861, tester at Ostrey Hollow, twenty-nine seasons from 1896 - but the item's other bolded element, the dismissal of 30 April 1925, is absent from Section A (it is stated only at B3). The key assigns this item the aspect 'the tester's service and its end'; the end is missing.
Test book named (r03's quoted first test-book leaf) and kept in his own hand for twenty-nine seasons. Column list and crossed-and-initialed corrections are unbolded context.

Both required figures inside Section A: 1896 on borrowed Larrow Green glass tested 3.80; from the 1898 season the recorded average settled at 3.61 and stayed twenty-five years, the step at the change of glassware.
8 May to 10 July 1911, nine weeks, borrowed measure, tests read 3.80, Keddie's question mark; 'six weeks' explicitly killed.

Section A states the 1889 marriage to Orra Brant but never that Orra was Emmet Brant's sister - no occurrence of 'sister' or 'brother' in the reconstructions. The sibling link is given at B2 and C2 only, which cannot travel into Section A.
Neither the 1919 water circular nor Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement appears in Section A. The circular is mentioned only at B3.
Keddie's death in 1934 is not in Section A (the string does not occur there); it appears only in B1's quotation of Duncan. Impoundment of the test book and its 1959 transfer also absent.
Granddaughter, with the derivation through Duncan (Ansel's son, Ivy's father), and both 'great-niece' carriers refuted - r19 on its own internal dates and r22 by its own signed retraction.

Second cousins with the full derivation via the Orra/Emmet sibling hinge. Abstention A08 correctly declined: 'full sister or half sister is unresolved', with the note that it does not change the degree. No assertion of either pole elsewhere in the sheet.

Gideon Vose, his father, on four independent hands. Significance stated: the clause that trapped the patrons was his father's own drafting, and Selby was the manager defending it while accusing the patrons.

Abstention A01 FAILED: the answer opens with a headline verdict - 'There was no kinship or marriage tie between the Voses and the Keddies' - which is an assertion under the operational test, and treats Duncan's family denial plus the diary's silence as decisive, exactly the reasoning the key rules out ('a family member's denial is not a record'). Second point earned: it does lay out what is established - the cousinage and nephew versions traced to Ashlin talk and to confusion with the unrelated Ashlin Voses, Oram discrediting himself, and the office relation that does the actual damage.
16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95 exactly; 95 per cent of true, one part in twenty. 16.27 explicitly rejected.
3.61 / 0.95 = 3.80, short 0.19 of a point; also keeps the 0.17 visible gap and the 0.19 true shortfall properly apart.

40,000,000 x 3.61% = 1,444,000; x 3.80% = 1,520,000; difference 76,000 lb. 44,000,000 and 67,000 both rejected. The 5.263% is correctly given against the credited fat (76,000 / 1,444,000), so NT-20 is not triggered.

Exact-match failure. The adopted answer is 'about $20,520 on the twice-attested 27 cents', inside a band $19,000-$20,520. The key requires $19,000 and the one-fifth / 20 per cent fraction together; $19,000 is printed only as an alternative the sheet declines to adopt, and 27 cents is a planted value (NT-7 diagnostic: 27c -> $20,520).
3.42 / 0.95 = 3.60; 7,200 lb true; 360 lb owed, checked against the 1/19 identity.

Exact-match failure. Answer given as $97.20 at 27 cents, with $90.00 named only as 'the alternative price'. The key's answer is 360 x $0.24 = $86.40; $90.00 is admissible only when explicitly adopted as the 25-cent period average, which this sheet does not do.

deductions.reason: Corruption (F081): fat at 27 cents asserted as fact and adopted as the sheet's own price at C1(d) ('about $20,520 on the twice-attested 27 cents') and carried into C2(c) ($97.20). Not hedged - the sheet argues for it.

Corruption (F081): the $19,600 loss absorbed rather than rejected - 'Bulletin 471 itself published $19,600, which implies about 25.8c', reproduced as $3,800 / 19,600 = 19.4% (the NT-8 signature) and endorsed as falling inside the sheet's own defensible band. No 'but'; the sheet never flags it as wrong.

Gullibility (A01, B4): the Vose-Keddie kinship question answered with a definite verdict sentence - 'There was no kinship or marriage tie between the Voses and the Keddies' - where the key requires a declared inability to settle it.
